# Row 80, 80 Howard Street, Yarmouth, Norfolk. 1861 census.
# THE FATHER IS NOT IN THE HOUSE. His wife is enumerated as HEAD and MARRIED, with her
# occupation ending in "wife" - at a fishing port on census night that ordinarily means
# a mariner at sea. SO THE BROTHER IS STILL NOT NAMED.
# Sarah Ann Bloom's birth registration, Yarmouth Q3 1853, vol 4B p1, gives the mother's
# maiden name as MORT - so this Sarah Bloom, born Yarmouth 1817, is Sarah née Mort.
# 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — THE HUSBAND HUNTED, AND A CANDIDATE FOUND BUT NOT PROVED.
# THREE ROUTES WERE TRIED. THE FIRST TWO FAILED AND THE REASONS ARE WORTH KEEPING.
# 1. THE MARRIAGE. Sarah's maiden name is MORT, from her daughter's 1853 birth registration.
#    Findmypast's marriage index will not search on a spouse's surname before 1912, so Bloom x Mort
#    cannot be asked directly. Asked the other way — SARAH MORT, marrying 1841 to 1851 — the index
#    returns five women and EVERY ONE IS IN LANCASHIRE OR CHESHIRE. MORT IS A LANCASHIRE SURNAME.
#    Either she married before civil registration, or MORT is a mis-reading of a longer name on that
#    birth entry. THE MAIDEN NAME THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN WORKING FROM IS NOW ITSELF IN DOUBT.
# 2. THE 1851 CENSUS AT GREAT YARMOUTH. Surname BLOOM: ONE result in the whole town, and it is an
#    ELIZABETH BLOOM FIELD — Bloomfield, not Bloom. The family is not there under that spelling,
#    although James was born at Yarmouth in 1848 and so they were in the town three years earlier.
# 3. THE 1871 CENSUS AT GREAT YARMOUTH — and this one produced a candidate.
#    RG10 piece 1784, folio 36, page 30, schedule 176, "Row, Great Yarmouth":
#       JAMES BLOOM   Head   52   born Yarmouth 1819   OCCUPATION: MARINER
#       Ann Bloom     Wife        born 1826
#       Robert Bloom  Son         born 1856
#       Alfred Bloom  Son         born 1858
#       Alice Bloom   Daughter    born 1860
# WHY HE IS A CANDIDATE: HE IS A MARINER, which is exactly what the 1861 household implied — a wife
# enumerated as head and married, occupation ending in "wife", at a fishing port on census night.
# AND TWO OF THE CHILDREN MATCH: ROBERT born 1856 and a son born 1858 are in both houses. The 1861
# return calls the 1858 boy ALLAN and the 1871 return calls him ALFRED.
# WHY IT IS NOT PROVED, AND THIS ARCHIVE IS NOT GOING TO ROUND IT UP:
#   THE WIFE'S NAME IS WRONG. 1861 has SARAH, 44, born Yarmouth 1817. 1871 has ANN, born 1826.
#   THE ADDRESS IS DIFFERENT. 80 Howard Street in 1861; a Row in 1871.
#   JAMES AND BLOOM ARE BOTH COMMON, and Yarmouth was full of mariners.
# TWO READINGS FIT. Either Sarah died between 1861 and 1871 and James remarried an Ann — which would
# make this the same family and name the brother-in-law of William Wear at last — OR there were two
# Bloom mariner households in one town. THE 1861 PAGE AT 80 HOWARD STREET AND THE DEATH INDEX FOR A
# SARAH BLOOM AT YARMOUTH IN THE 1860s WOULD DECIDE IT. Neither has been read.
